websites.hook: A website that makes your business easy to understand.
websites.problemHeadline: Your website should answer the questions customers bring.

pains.title: An unclear story
pains.body: Visitors have to piece together what you do and whether it is right for them.

pains.title: A disconnected journey
pains.body: The site looks finished, but enquiries, bookings or publishing still need manual work.

pains.title: A site nobody can own
pains.body: Every small update becomes another request to a developer.

benefits.title: Help visitors understand the offer
benefits.body: We put the business, services and next step in a clear order, so visitors can find what matters to them.

benefits.title: Keep the design and build connected
benefits.body: We take the pages from content and design through development, including the forms and tools they depend on.

benefits.title: Manage the site after launch
benefits.body: Your team receives the agreed editing access and guidance for publishing content and managing the site.

websites.solutionHeadline: A complete website, from the page plan to launch.
scopeHeadlines: Explain the business. Make it recognizable.
Build the journey. Prepare the launch.
websites.alternative: If the foundation still works, a focused repair may be enough.
websites.firstCheckpoint: First checkpoint: agree the pages, content and design direction before building out the site.

ecommerce.hook: Build a store that works for customers and your team.
ecommerce.problemHeadline: The buying experience and store operations need to fit together.

pains.title: An inconsistent buying experience
pains.body: The brand, product pages and checkout journey feel like separate projects.

pains.title: Too much manual upkeep
pains.body: Catalog, inventory and customer data move between disconnected tools.

pains.title: A launch with loose ends
pains.body: The site is ready, but channels, notifications or store operations are not.

benefits.title: Bring the launch together
benefits.body: Your brand, product catalog and shopping pages are planned together, with the launch requirements in one scope.

benefits.title: Connect the work behind the store
benefits.body: We link the agreed inventory, email, SMS and business tools, then check how data moves between them.

benefits.title: Know how the store works
benefits.body: Test orders and the handover cover the buying journeys and operating tasks your team will use.

ecommerce.solutionHeadline: Your brand, products and store operations in one build.
scopeHeadlines: Build the brand and the store together.
Connect the buying journey to your operations.
Improve, migrate or connect the store.
ecommerce.alternative: A working store may need one improvement rather than a full rebuild.
ecommerce.firstCheckpoint: First checkpoint: agree the storefront, data mappings and order scenarios before building the store.

software-solutions.hook: Build software around the way your business works.
software-solutions.problemHeadline: Your team should not have to work around the tools.

pains.title: A fragmented experience
pains.body: Customers, staff and owners work across tools that were never designed together.

pains.title: A prototype without a path to launch
pains.body: The idea is visible, but accounts, data, integrations and operations remain unfinished.

pains.title: Unclear ownership
pains.body: You need to know who controls the code, deployment and data after delivery.

benefits.title: Give customers a connected experience
benefits.body: The product website, accounts and application are designed around the same customer journey.

benefits.title: Include the tools to run the product
benefits.body: The build covers the agreed admin operations, data and integrations as well as the customer-facing features.

benefits.title: Keep control after delivery
benefits.body: You receive the commissioned code, deployment and data under the agreed terms. Ongoing support is optional.

software-solutions.solutionHeadline: The product people use and the tools you need to run it.
scopeHeadlines: Connect the first visit to the product.
Build for customers and the people running it.
Connect the data. Hand over the product.
software-solutions.alternative: If the idea still needs testing, start with a prototype or one working flow.
software-solutions.firstCheckpoint: First checkpoint: review the architecture, interface and a working slice before extending the product.

ai-solutions.hook: Give AI a real job in your business.
ai-solutions.problemHeadline: An agent needs to work beyond the demo.

pains.title: The agent lacks the right context
pains.body: The instructions are there, but the information needed to complete the task is missing.

pains.title: Disconnected tools
pains.body: People still move inputs and outputs between the agent and the systems they use.

pains.title: Results are hard to assess
pains.body: There is no agreed way to check the output, handle mistakes or approve important actions.

benefits.title: Find out what works on your task
benefits.body: We test realistic inputs and the uncertain model or tool behavior before building the wider workflow.

benefits.title: Choose what the agent can do
benefits.body: Tool access, permissions and review steps define where the agent can act and where your team stays involved.

benefits.title: See how the system is performing
benefits.body: Evaluation, cost limits and recovery are part of the scope, so the operator can inspect results and manage runs.

ai-solutions.solutionHeadline: An agent connected to the work, with checks built in.
scopeHeadlines: Put the agent where the work happens.
Build around the tools and evidence it needs.
Connect the agent to the application.
ai-solutions.alternative: If you need product configuration rather than a custom build, start with AI setup.
ai-solutions.firstCheckpoint: First checkpoint: test the task, tools and uncertain model behavior against examples of a useful result.

agent-teams.hook: Give complex work to a coordinated team of agents.
agent-teams.problemHeadline: More agents should not mean more work to coordinate.

pains.title: Work without clear ownership
pains.body: Tasks overlap or disappear between agents with loosely defined roles.

pains.title: Context lost at handoff
pains.body: Each worker starts again because the relevant information does not travel with the job.

pains.title: Separate outputs still need checking
pains.body: The workers finish their parts, but someone still has to review and combine the result.

benefits.title: Give each agent a clear job
benefits.body: We map the work and assign roles before connecting the manager and specialist workers.

benefits.title: Carry context through the handoffs
benefits.body: Each role receives the information and tool permissions it needs, with rules for handing work over or raising a problem.

benefits.title: Review the combined result
benefits.body: The manager checks and combines worker outputs. Failed and blocked jobs remain visible so they can be recovered.

agent-teams.solutionHeadline: A manager, specialist workers and a reviewed result.
scopeHeadlines: Build the team around the workflow.
agent-teams.alternative: If one agent can do the job, a team may add unnecessary complexity.
agent-teams.firstCheckpoint: First checkpoint: map the roles, handoffs and permissions before implementing the team.

agent-infrastructure.hook: Run your agents with the tools and controls they need.
agent-infrastructure.problemHeadline: A working agent also needs a way to be operated.

pains.title: Execution tied to a local setup
pains.body: The agent works in development but has no defined deployment or operating path.

pains.title: Failures are hard to inspect
pains.body: Task state, tool calls and retries are difficult to follow or recover.

pains.title: Controls added too late
pains.body: Permissions, usage limits and operator responsibilities are still undefined.

benefits.title: Use an environment that fits the agent
benefits.body: We assess the existing harness or build the execution loop, tool interfaces and state the task requires.

benefits.title: Understand what happened in a run
benefits.body: Task state, logs and error handling give operators a way to inspect failures and recover work.

benefits.title: Set the operating limits
benefits.body: Permissions, time limits and usage controls are defined as part of the build, with responsibilities recorded for handover.

agent-infrastructure.solutionHeadline: An operating environment for the agent you want to run.
scopeHeadlines: Build the environment. Define the controls.
agent-infrastructure.alternative: If an existing harness fits, we can configure and deploy it rather than build another.
agent-infrastructure.firstCheckpoint: First checkpoint: agree the runtime, tool access and operating limits before building or deploying the harness.

jev-implementation.hook: Give repeated decisions a clear place in your workflow.
jev-implementation.problemHeadline: Your software needs to know what happens after a decision.

pains.title: Unstructured decisions
pains.body: Your application needs a defined category or route, rather than another open-ended answer.

pains.title: No rule for uncertain results
pains.body: The workflow needs to distinguish a result it can use from one that needs another route or a review.

pains.title: An integration without evaluation
pains.body: The decision logic has not been compared with representative, reviewed examples.

benefits.title: Get a result the application can use
benefits.body: We define the decision schema and connect its output to the next step in your system.

benefits.title: Decide when to ask for review
benefits.body: Thresholds and fallback paths specify what happens when confidence is low or the provider is unavailable.

benefits.title: Check the decision on your examples
benefits.body: We compare results with reviewed inputs before you use the integration to control the workflow.

jev-implementation.solutionHeadline: A tested decision connected to the next action.
scopeHeadlines: Turn context into an actionable decision.
Evaluate the result. Define the fallback.
jev-implementation.alternative: Jev is for structured decisions. Text or media generation needs a different model.
jev-implementation.firstCheckpoint: First checkpoint: define the possible decisions and review example inputs before connecting Jev.

context-and-memory.hook: Give your agents the context they keep missing.
context-and-memory.problemHeadline: The information exists. The agent needs a way to use it.

pains.title: The same briefing, again
pains.body: People repeat information because an agent does not retain the context it needs.

pains.title: Sources that are hard to find
pains.body: Important business knowledge is spread across documents and systems.

pains.title: Information without clear rules
pains.body: Freshness, access, updates and deletion are not consistently defined.

benefits.title: Use the knowledge your business already has
benefits.body: We organize the sources, instructions and task context your agents need, with access agreed by the source owners.

benefits.title: Check what the agent can find
benefits.body: We test retrieval against real questions, rather than treating a connected database as a finished result.

benefits.title: Keep the information manageable
benefits.body: The system includes rules for updating, accessing and deleting the context that is stored.

context-and-memory.solutionHeadline: Business knowledge your agents can retrieve and use.
scopeHeadlines: Organize, retrieve and maintain the context.
context-and-memory.alternative: A vector database is one option. We choose storage and search for the task.
context-and-memory.firstCheckpoint: First checkpoint: inventory the sources and test questions, then agree storage, retrieval and access rules.

mcp-and-api.hook: Connect the tools your work depends on.
mcp-and-api.problemHeadline: Your team should not be the connection between every system.

pains.title: Manual transfer between systems
pains.body: People copy data or repeat actions because applications do not share a working interface.

pains.title: Private tools beyond the agent’s reach
pains.body: A useful business system has no supported agent-facing connection.

pains.title: Access without clear boundaries
pains.body: Authentication, permitted actions and failure behavior need to be defined together.

benefits.title: Build the connection you need
benefits.body: We use an existing integration when it fits, or create the missing interface for your system.

benefits.title: Control what can be accessed
benefits.body: Authentication, validation and permissions define the actions each client is allowed to perform.

benefits.title: Give the owner usable documentation
benefits.body: The handover covers the interface, deployment and operating checks so your team can work with the connection.

mcp-and-api.solutionHeadline: A working connection with permissions and failure handling.
scopeHeadlines: Connect existing tools or build the missing interface.
Bring the connection into the product.
mcp-and-api.alternative: If a supported connection already exists, we can configure and verify it instead.
mcp-and-api.firstCheckpoint: First checkpoint: agree the actions, data and access rules before implementing the interface.

creative-ai-workflows.hook: Build a repeatable process for image, video and audio.
creative-ai-workflows.problemHeadline: Generating a file is only part of producing usable work.

pains.title: A brief lost between tools
pains.body: Brand context and references do not reliably follow the work into generation.

pains.title: Review scattered across files
pains.body: Versions, feedback and approvals become difficult to track.

pains.title: Delivery still done by hand
pains.body: Jobs finish, but outputs still need organizing, checking and exporting.

benefits.title: Keep the brief with the work
benefits.body: Brand assets, references and intended placements carry into the generation workflow.

benefits.title: Keep your reviewer involved
benefits.body: Version tracking and explicit review steps give the team a way to assess and refine the outputs.

benefits.title: Deliver files in the formats you need
benefits.body: We connect the agreed export and delivery steps, including checks for file types and dimensions.

creative-ai-workflows.solutionHeadline: Connect the brief, generation, review and delivery.
scopeHeadlines: Carry the brief into image and video production.
Connect audio, agents and final review.
creative-ai-workflows.alternative: This builds the production workflow. Ongoing content production is a separate engagement.
creative-ai-workflows.firstCheckpoint: First checkpoint: test available models against your briefs and required output formats.

ai-setup-and-consulting.hook: Help your team get useful work from AI.
ai-setup-and-consulting.problemHeadline: An account is a starting point, not a working setup.

pains.title: Accounts without a working process
pains.body: The team has access, but no defined workflow to configure or try.

pains.title: A setup that does not connect
pains.body: The right context, repository or business tools are missing from the environment.

pains.title: An uncertain handover
pains.body: Users do not know how to operate the setup or what it will cost to run.

benefits.title: Choose a setup for the work
benefits.body: We establish the intended workflow and verify the exact product, account and supported access.

benefits.title: Connect what the team needs
benefits.body: Instructions, business context and agreed tool connections are configured around realistic tasks.

benefits.title: Know how to use it
benefits.body: A walkthrough and usage guidance cover the setup, operating controls and ongoing costs.

ai-setup-and-consulting.solutionHeadline: A configured environment your team knows how to use.
scopeHeadlines: Configure the environment around the workflow.
Verify the product, access and setup path.
ai-setup-and-consulting.alternative: If you need a new application or custom agent, we scope that as a separate build.
ai-setup-and-consulting.firstCheckpoint: First checkpoint: verify the product, account and access needed for your intended workflow.

brand.hook: Make your brand recognizable wherever customers meet it.
brand.problemHeadline: The same business should feel like the same brand.

pains.title: An identity that feels unfinished
pains.body: The logo exists, but typography, imagery and applications do not hold together.

pains.title: Guidelines without usable assets
pains.body: The team still improvises every new page, document or campaign.

pains.title: The design has not reached the product
pains.body: The approved identity still needs to be applied to the website, store or software.

benefits.title: Agree the direction before wider production
benefits.body: We use representative applications to show how the brand will work in context.

benefits.title: Give your team a usable kit
benefits.body: Organized assets, templates and guidance help the people making your next page, product or document.

benefits.title: Carry the identity into the build
benefits.body: When implementation is included, we apply the brand to the website, store or software and review the result there.

brand.solutionHeadline: A visual identity with the assets to put it to work.
scopeHeadlines: Define the identity. Make it usable.
Carry the brand into its real applications.
brand.alternative: If the identity is already right, we can focus on implementation.
brand.firstCheckpoint: First checkpoint: agree the brand direction through representative applications before producing the wider kit.

unslop.hook: Bring the work up to the standard of your business.
unslop.problemHeadline: You have a starting point. Now it needs a considered finish.

pains.title: Design that could belong to anyone
pains.body: Generic layouts and inconsistent branding weaken the character of the work.

pains.title: Copy that does not say enough
pains.body: Repetition and vague language obscure the business and its offer.

pains.title: A journey that breaks down
pains.body: The pages look complete, but the mobile layout, forms or next steps fall short.

benefits.title: Preserve the work that holds up
benefits.body: We inspect the pages, copy and customer journeys before deciding what needs to change.

benefits.title: See the direction before wider changes
benefits.body: A representative correction gives you something concrete to review before the remaining repairs.

benefits.title: Check the result in use
benefits.body: We recheck affected pages and journeys and preserve your business facts as the work is revised.

unslop.solutionHeadline: Improve the work you have with a defined repair scope.
scopeHeadlines: Preserve the foundation. Repair the experience.
Set a clear standard for the writing and the work.
unslop.alternative: If the foundation needs replacing, we’ll explain why a repair is not enough.
unslop.firstCheckpoint: First checkpoint: review one representative correction before applying the direction across the remaining scope.

consultation.hook: Know what to build, fix or change next.
consultation.problemHeadline: Make the next commitment with the important questions answered.

pains.title: Too many plausible options
pains.body: Platforms, architectures or suppliers offer different tradeoffs without a clear recommendation.

pains.title: A problem without a diagnosis
pains.body: Symptoms are visible, but the evidence does not yet explain the cause.

pains.title: A proposal with unanswered questions
pains.body: Dependencies, ownership or acceptance remain unclear before work begins.

benefits.title: Focus the review on your decision
benefits.body: We agree the questions and inspection scope before the work starts.

benefits.title: Understand the tradeoffs
benefits.body: The assessment explains the evidence, assumptions, options and gaps that matter to the decision.

benefits.title: Use the plan with the team you choose
benefits.body: The written recommendation and next steps are yours to take to Fortitudo, your team or another provider.

consultation.solutionHeadline: A written recommendation you can act on.
scopeHeadlines: Turn the objective or problem into a plan.
Review the technical and customer experience.
Clarify the implementation before committing.
consultation.alternative: The review stands on its own. You do not have to hire us to implement it.
consultation.firstCheckpoint: First checkpoint: agree the questions, access and written output before the review begins.
